concepts.name: Andes
concepts.definition: The world's longest continental mountain range, running about 8,900 km down South America's western edge through seven countries and topping out at Aconcagua.

concepts.name: Rocky Mountains
concepts.definition: North America's largest mountain system, stretching about 4,800 km from British Columbia to New Mexico, peaking at Colorado's Mount Elbert.

concepts.name: Appalachian Mountains
concepts.definition: Ancient mountain range in eastern North America, extending about 3,300 km from Newfoundland to central Alabama, highest at North Carolina's Mount Mitchell.

concepts.name: Alps
concepts.definition: Europe's highest and most extensive mountain range, arcing about 1,200 km through France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria and neighbouring countries, crowned by Mont Blanc.

concepts.name: Pyrenees
concepts.definition: Mountain range in southwestern Europe extending nearly 500 km along the France–Spain border, forming the natural boundary between the two countries.

concepts.name: Carpathians
concepts.definition: Europe's third-longest mountain range, arcing about 1,500 km across Central and Southeast Europe around the Transylvanian Plateau, mostly within Romania.

concepts.name: Apennines
concepts.definition: Mountain range of parallel chains running about 1,200 km down the length of peninsular Italy, highest at Corno Grande in the Gran Sasso massif.

concepts.name: Atlas Mountains
concepts.definition: Mountain range in the Maghreb of North Africa, stretching about 2,500 km through Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia and separating the Sahara from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts.

concepts.name: Ural Mountains
concepts.definition: North-south mountain range running about 2,500 km through Russia into Kazakhstan, forming part of the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia.

concepts.name: Himalayas
concepts.definition: Asia's great mountain range, arcing about 2,400 km across Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan and holding Earth's highest peaks, including Mount Everest.

concepts.name: Karakoram
concepts.definition: Mountain range in the Kashmir region spanning Pakistan, China and India, home to K2 and the most heavily glaciated terrain outside the polar regions.

concepts.name: Hindu Kush
concepts.definition: About 800-km-long mountain range in Central and South Asia west of the Himalayas, running through Afghanistan, Pakistan and Tajikistan; highest peak Tirich Mir.

concepts.name: Tian Shan
concepts.definition: Large mountain system of Central Asia spanning Kyrgyzstan, China, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, north of the Taklamakan Desert; highest peak Jengish Chokusu.

concepts.name: Altai Mountains
concepts.definition: Mountain range in Central Asia where Russia, China, Mongolia and Kazakhstan converge, forming the headwaters of the Irtysh and Ob rivers; highest peak Belukha.

concepts.name: Zagros Mountains
concepts.definition: Fold mountain range about 1,600 km long across Iran, Iraq and Turkey, forming the barrier between the Mesopotamian Plain and the Iranian plateau; highest peak Mount Dena.

concepts.name: Great Dividing Range
concepts.definition: Australia's largest mountain system, running over 3,500 km along the eastern coast and serving as the main watershed for eastern Australia's rivers.

concepts.name: Drakensberg
concepts.definition: Escarpment mountain range over 1,000 km long forming the eastern edge of southern Africa's plateau across South Africa and Lesotho; highest peak Thabana Ntlenyana.

concepts.name: Ethiopian Highlands
concepts.definition: Rugged mountain mass in northeast Africa across Ethiopia and Eritrea, the continent's largest continuous elevated region.

concepts.name: Alaska Range
concepts.definition: Mountain range in south-central Alaska housing Denali, North America's highest peak, extending into Yukon, Canada.

concepts.name: Annamite Range
concepts.definition: Mountain range running along the Laos-Vietnam border, separating the Mekong basin from Vietnam's narrow coastal plain.

concepts.name: Brooks Range
concepts.definition: Mountain range across northern Alaska and Yukon marking North America's northernmost continental divide and the Arctic tree line.

concepts.name: Cascade Range
concepts.definition: Volcanic mountain range from British Columbia through Washington and Oregon to Northern California, part of the Pacific Ring of Fire.

concepts.name: Caucasus Mountains
concepts.definition: Mountain system between the Black and Caspian Seas forming a traditional boundary between Europe and Asia, home to Mount Elbrus.

concepts.name: Coast Mountains
concepts.definition: Mountain range along the Pacific coast from southwestern Yukon through Alaska's panhandle to British Columbia.

concepts.name: Ellsworth Mountains
concepts.definition: Antarctica's highest mountain range, a 350-km chain on the western Ronne Ice Shelf margin containing Mount Vinson, the continent's tallest peak.

concepts.name: Greater Khingan
concepts.definition: Volcanic mountain range in Inner Mongolia, China, and eastern Mongolia dividing the Amur and Nen-Songhua river drainage systems.

concepts.name: Kunlun Mountains
concepts.definition: One of Asia's longest ranges, stretching over 3,000 km across western China and forming the Tibetan Plateau's northern boundary.

concepts.name: Pamir Mountains
concepts.definition: Central Asian mountain knot known as the 'Roof of the World,' linking the Tian Shan, Karakoram, Kunlun, and Himalayas.

concepts.name: Pensacola Mountains
concepts.definition: Group of Antarctic mountain ranges in Queen Elizabeth Land spanning 450 km within the Transantarctic Mountains system.

concepts.name: Queen Maud Mountains
concepts.definition: Section of the Transantarctic Mountains between the Beardmore and Reedy Glaciers, named by Roald Amundsen during his 1911 South Pole expedition.

concepts.name: Sivalik Hills
concepts.definition: Outermost, southernmost range of the Himalayan foothills stretching 2,400 km across India, Nepal, and Pakistan, rich in fossil beds.

concepts.name: Stanovoy Range
concepts.definition: Mountain system in Far Eastern Russia dividing Arctic and Pacific Ocean watersheds, the historic Russia-China border from 1689 to 1858.

concepts.name: Transantarctic Mountains
concepts.definition: One of Earth's longest mountain ranges, stretching 3,500 km across Antarctica and dividing the continent into eastern and western regions.
